pr_completion:
There is no "complete now" call. In mcp__azure-devops__repo_pull_request_write, action "update", the status enum is only "Active" or "Abandoned" (Abandoned closes the PR without merging; treat it as outward too). A PR is completed only through auto-complete:
{action:"update", repositoryId, pullRequestId, project?, autoComplete:true, mergeStrategy?:"NoFastForward"|"Squash"|"Rebase"|"RebaseMerge", mergeCommitMessage?, deleteSourceBranch? (default false), transitionWorkItems? (default TRUE), bypassPolicy? (default false; true needs bypassReason)}.

From the 2.11.0 source (repositories.js lines 771-794), the server sets autoCompleteSetBy to the signed-in user's id and completionOptions to {deleteSourceBranch, transitionWorkItems: transitionWorkItems !== false, bypassPolicy, mergeStrategy?, mergeCommitMessage?, bypassReason?}. The zod schema also has .default(true). So when transitionWorkItems is absent it is true and ADO transitions the linked work items on merge. That is how #361691 was auto-closed and skipped QA.

- If every policy already passes, ADO merges at once, so autoComplete:true is the merge itself.
- autoComplete:false sets both autoCompleteSetBy and completionOptions to null, which cancels auto-complete. It is still a write.
- The completion fields are ignored unless autoComplete is true. Without mergeStrategy, ADO uses the branch or policy default.

Guard: classify action==="update" && autoComplete===true as merge-class, and status==="Abandoned" as abandon. Read the target from tool_input.pullRequestId and tool_input.repositoryId (a name or a GUID; a name needs project). Consider requiring an explicit transitionWorkItems:false, or warning when it is absent. To see the current auto-complete state first, call repo_pull_request with action "get", which returns the full PR including completionOptions.

Server 2 (2.10.0) handles these fields the same way. But its isDraft has a default of false that update copies, so any update there also publishes a draft PR.
work_item_state_change:
Use mcp__azure-devops__wit_work_item_write with action "update":
{action:"update", id:<number>, project?:"BigChange" (the server ignores it for update), updates:[{op:"test", path:"/rev", value:<rev>}, {op:"add"|"replace", path:"/fields/System.State", value:"Approval"}, {op:"add", path:"/fields/WEF_36778208447642C48B0A0F72C104A5C5_Kanban.Column", value:"Ready for testing"}, {op:"add", path:"/fields/Custom.Release#", value:"26.11.02"}]}

A real call from an earlier session:
{"action":"update","project":"BigChange","id":361339,"updates":[{"op":"test","path":"/rev","value":3},{"op":"add","path":"/fields/System.State","value":"Removed"}]}

- op is lowercased by the server and defaults to "add".
- value can be a string, number, boolean or null. Server 1 also accepts objects and arrays, for relations on /relations/-.

Other actions:
- Several items: {action:"update_batch", batchUpdates:[{id, op:"Add"|"Replace"|"Remove", path:"/fields/System.State", value:"<string>", format?}]}.
- New item: {action:"create", workItemType, fields:[{name:"System.State", value}, ...]}. Here name has no /fields/ prefix.
- add_child: items carry only title, description, format, areaPath and iterationPath, so it cannot set state.

Board column: Midas items carry three boards' fields. The Midas board is WEF_36778208447642C48B0A0F72C104A5C5. Its _Kanban.Column equals System.BoardColumn in all 71 items sampled from earlier reads, and the board also has _Kanban.Column.Done and _Kanban.Lane (lanes "Planned work" and "Support tickets"). The other two boards, WEF_3057C7889BA14D699C0145FC63698233 and WEF_238344A83E10404F9482A4EA1FE089FE, always show Backlog and New. State Approval spans the Reviewing, Ready for testing and Testing columns, so the guard must read both state and column.

How the guard reads the call:
- ids: update gives [Number(id)]; update_batch gives the unique batchUpdates[].id values; add_child gives [parentId]; create has no id yet. Coerce strings, because z.coerce accepts them.
- Target state: the value of the op whose lowercased path is "/fields/system.state". For create, the fields entry whose name is "System.State".
- Column change: a path matching /^\/fields\/(system\.boardcolumn|wef_[0-9a-f]{32}_kanban\.column(\.done)?)$/i.
- Lane change: a path matching /^\/fields\/(system\.boardlane|wef_[0-9a-f]{32}_kanban\.lane)$/i.
- Custom field: a path matching /^\/fields\/custom\./i (for example Custom.Release#).
- Field names are case-insensitive in ADO, so lowercase before comparing.

These other calls also change items: repo_pull_request_write update with autoComplete (through transitionWorkItems), wit_backlog reorder, wit_work_item_link_write, wit_work_item_attachment_link, testplan_test_case_write update_steps, and wit_work_item_comment_write.
pipeline_run:
Queue a run with mcp__azure-devops__pipelines_write:
{action:"run_pipeline", project, pipelineId, pipelineVersion?, resources?:{repositories:{self:{refName:"refs/heads/<branch>", version?}}, pipelines:{<alias>:{runId|version}}, builds, containers, packages}, templateParameters?:{k:"v"}, variables?:{k:{value,isSecret}}, stagesToSkip?:[...], previewRun?:true, yamlOverride?}
This sends a POST to pipelines/{id}/runs. With previewRun:true it returns the expanded YAML and creates no run. yamlOverride is only allowed with previewRun.

Cancel, retry or run one stage:
{action:"update_build_stage", project, buildId, stageName, status:"Cancel"|"Retry"|"Run", forceRetryAllJobs? (default false)}
This sends a PATCH to _apis/build/builds/{buildId}/stages/{stageName} with body {forceRetryAllJobs, state}. There is no whole-build cancel or retry; re-queueing means another run_pipeline.

Definition changes: create_pipeline (name, yamlPath, repositoryType, repositoryName, repositoryId, folder) and rename_pipeline (pipelineId, name).

Approving gates: no tool on either server can. The 2.11.0 source has no timeline, approvals or checkpoint call anywhere. Status "Run" starts a manual or skipped stage and does not approve a check; that is from ADO docs and was not tested here. Gate approval stays a browser action: Review then Resume for ManualValidation@0 on pipeline 1274, and the environment approval for BatchDataProcess prod. Alternatively it is a REST call outside MCP, which only a Bash guard would catch.

pipelines_run (get, list) and pipelines_build are reads despite their names. The schemas are identical on server 2.
hidden_writes: repo_create_branch: always (no action param). It creates a branch ref on the server, which is the same as a push.
wiki_upsert_page: always (no action param). It creates or edits a wiki page, which is a commit to the wiki repo (branch wikiMaster by default).
wit_work_item_attachment_upload: always, server 1 only. It uploads file content to the ADO attachment store, even if the file is never linked to an item.
wit_work_item_attachment_link: always, server 1 only. It adds an AttachedFile relation to a work item.
wit_backlog, action reorder, both servers. It moves items in the team backlog or in an iteration, which rewrites their order.

Local disk only, no ADO write: pipelines_artifact with action download and destinationPath, and wit_work_item_attachment with savePath. Both save files under the MCP server's working directory. agentic-midas's guard asks before these.

today_queries.need: (1) My work items by board column in area BigChange\Finance\Midas
today_queries.action_and_params: wit_query {action:'wiql', project:'BigChange', top:200, wiql:`SELECT [System.Id] FROM WorkItems WHERE [System.TeamProject] = 'BigChange' AND [System.AreaPath] UNDER 'BigChange\Finance\Midas' AND [System.AssignedTo] = @Me AND [System.State] NOT IN ('Closed','Removed')`} returns ids. Then wit_work_item {action:'get_batch', project:'BigChange', ids:[...], fields:['System.Id','System.Title','System.WorkItemType','System.State','System.BoardColumn','System.BoardColumnDone','System.BoardLane','System.ChangedDate']}, and group by System.BoardColumn in code.
today_queries.limitation: wiql returns only ids, and top defaults to 50, so always pass top. get_batch takes at most 200 ids per call (ADO limit) and needs a project. For items in this area, System.BoardColumn is the Midas board's column. Memory notes that 'IN @TeamAreas' and CONTAINS on area paths are rejected, while UNDER works. The wit_work_item action 'my' is project-wide (not filtered by area) and capped at top 50, and which fields it returns is unverified.

today_queries.need: (2) PRs where I am a reviewer and have not voted
today_queries.limitation: Returns active PRs only, across all projects. top and skip apply before the vote filter. 'pending' keeps PRs where my own reviewer entry has vote 0. A PR that lists only a team I belong to has no entry for me, so it is dropped, and whether ADO's reviewerId search matches through group membership at all is unverified. Waiting for author (-5) and rejected (-10) count as voted. Drafts are included; the output has isDraft. Server 2 has no org tool, and its repo_pull_request list drops reviewers, so it would need a list plus one get per PR.

today_queries.need: (3) Teammates' items in board column 'Ready for testing'
today_queries.action_and_params: wit_query {action:'wiql', project:'BigChange', top:200, wiql:`SELECT [System.Id] FROM WorkItems WHERE [System.AreaPath] UNDER 'BigChange\Finance\Midas' AND [System.BoardColumn] = 'Ready for testing' AND [System.AssignedTo] <> @Me`}. Then get_batch with fields ['System.Id','System.Title','System.WorkItemType','System.AssignedTo','System.State','System.BoardColumn','System.ChangedDate','Microsoft.VSTS.Common.StateChangeDate'].
today_queries.limitation: Filter on BoardColumn, not State, because state Approval covers Reviewing, Ready for testing and Testing. No field records when an item entered a column; that needs wit_work_item list_revisions for each item. How '<> @Me' treats unassigned items is unverified. The column text must match exactly.

today_queries.action_and_params: wit_query {action:'wiql', project:'BigChange', top:200, timePrecision:true, wiql:`SELECT [System.Id] FROM WorkItems WHERE [System.AreaPath] UNDER 'BigChange\Finance\Midas' AND [System.WorkItemType] = 'Platform Support' AND [System.State] = 'New'`}. To get items created since a stored time, use AND [System.CreatedDate] > '<last-seen ISO time>' instead. Then get_batch with fields ['System.Id','System.Title','System.State','System.BoardColumn','System.BoardLane','System.CreatedDate','System.CreatedBy','System.AssignedTo'].
today_queries.limitation: 'Platform Support' is a work item type. In this area it uses lane 'Support tickets', states New, Active and Closed, and columns New, Implementing and Done. 'New since I last looked' needs a timestamp the plugin stores itself. If items are raised in another area and moved in, they only show up after the move; where triage happens is unverified.

today_queries.need: (5) Pipeline runs waiting at a ManualValidation or approval gate, and since when
today_queries.action_and_params: {action:'list', project:'BigChange', definitions:[1274, <others>], statusFilter:1, queryOrder:'StartTimeDescending', top:50}. statusFilter 1 is InProgress. It returns in-progress builds with queueTime, startTime, sourceBranch and requestedFor.
today_queries.limitation: Neither server can answer this. No tool reads the build timeline (_apis/build/builds/{id}/timeline, where an inProgress record of type Checkpoint.Approval or a ManualValidation task has a startTime that means 'waiting since'). No tool reads the approvals API (_apis/pipelines/approvals?state=pending, which has createdOn). get_status returns the build report, and pipelines_run returns only run state and createdDate, so a build stopped at a gate looks the same as one that is running. Answering this needs a REST call outside MCP. The Azure CLI is not installed, and whether the git credential token works on build endpoints is unverified.

today_queries.tool: mcp__azure-devops__wit_query and wit_work_item, plus repo_pull_request for an exact check
today_queries.action_and_params: wit_query {action:'wiql', project:'BigChange', top:200, wiql:`SELECT [System.Id] FROM WorkItems WHERE [System.AreaPath] UNDER 'BigChange\Finance\Midas' AND [System.WorkItemType] IN ('Bug','Enabler','User Story') AND ([System.BoardColumn] IN ('Ready for testing','Testing') OR [System.State] = 'Closed') AND [System.ChangedDate] >= @Today - 30 AND [System.ExternalLinkCount] > 0 AND [Custom.Release#] = ''`}. Then get_batch with 'Custom.Release#' among the fields. To prove the merge for each item: wit_work_item {action:'get', id, expand:'Relations'}, find ArtifactLink relations named 'Pull Request' (vstfs:///Git/PullRequestId/{projectId}%2F{repoId}%2F{prId}), then repo_pull_request {action:'get', repositoryId:<repo GUID>, pullRequestId, project:'BigChange'} and check for status Completed (3) with a closedDate.
today_queries.limitation: WIQL cannot join on PR state, so 'merged' means either a column or state proxy, or a walk over PR links with one call per item and per PR. Two WIQL details are unverified: comparing [Custom.Release#] to '' and using '#' inside the bracketed field name. The field has been written through the API before as Custom.Release#. In the Midas flow the tester sets Release# while testing, so items in Ready for testing without it may be normal.

guard_regex_suggestion:
Outward tool names, anchored, for both servers:
/^mcp__(?:plugin_agentic-midas_)?azure-devops__(?:[a-z_]+_write|repo_create_branch|wiki_upsert_page|wit_work_item_attachment_(?:upload|link)|wit_backlog)$/
It matches 17 names on server 1 and 14 on server 2. I tested it in node against all 44 server-1 names and 40 server-2 names plus 4 decoys (draft_work_item, a prefixed name, a suffixed name, a read tool): no misses and no false hits.

Hook matcher for all ADO tools: ^mcp__(plugin_agentic-midas_)?azure-devops__ (the same prefix agentic-midas's register.tsx uses).

Per-action logic the hook still needs:
1. wit_backlog is outward only when tool_input.action === "reorder"; list and list_work_items are reads.
2. Every other matched name is outward for every action. Optionally, let pipelines_write run_pipeline with previewRun === true through, since it creates no run.
3. Fail closed. Server 1 is unpinned and can gain tools or actions after a restart. So treat any ADO-prefixed tool as outward unless it is on this read allowlist: advsec_get_alert_details, advsec_get_alerts, core_get_identity_ids, core_list_project_teams, core_list_projects, pipelines_artifact, pipelines_build, pipelines_build_log, pipelines_definition, pipelines_run, repo_branch, repo_file, repo_pull_request, repo_pull_request_org, repo_pull_request_thread, repo_repository, repo_search_commits, search_code, search_wiki, search_workitem, testplan, testplan_show_test_results_from_build_id, wiki, wit_backlog (minus reorder), wit_query, wit_work_item, wit_work_item_attachment, work, plus ping if the mcp-apps domain is ever enabled.
4. Sub-classes for the gate wording:
   - push: repo_create_branch, repo_file_write (and wiki_upsert_page if wanted)
   - merge: repo_pull_request_write with action update and autoComplete === true
   - abandon: status === "Abandoned"
   - pipeline: pipelines_write
   - work item: all the rest
5. mcp__agentic-midas__draft_work_item does not match and is not an ADO write.

Code to reuse: decide() in C:\Users\dev\.claude\plugins\cache\agentic-midas\agentic-midas\0.1.0\hooks\register.tsx already does this allowlist logic, including reorder, savePath and destinationPath. It only needs repo_pull_request_org added for 2.11.0.
server_differences:
Versions: server 1 runs `cmd /c npx -y @azure-devops/mcp bigchange`, which is unpinned. Its npx cache holds 2.11.0, installed 2026-10-22, in C:\Users\dev\AppData\Local
pm-cache\_npx\38bc830389a22c8c
ode_modules\@azure-devops\mcp, and the live schemas match that source. Server 2 is pinned to @azure-devops/mcp@2.10.0 with --authentication azcli (C:\Users\dev\AppData\Local
pm-cache\_npx\ec201a4708486269). The Azure CLI is not installed, so every server 2 call fails sign-in.

Only on server 1: repo_pull_request_org, repo_file_write, wit_work_item_attachment_upload and wit_work_item_attachment_link. Every other tool name exists on both servers, and both tool lists match their package source exactly.

repo_pull_request_write: same actions and the same completion fields on both, and transitionWorkItems defaults to true on both. But in 2.10.0, isDraft has a default of false and update copies it, so any update there (title, labels, autoComplete and so on) also publishes a draft PR. In 2.11.0, leaving isDraft out keeps the draft state.
wit_work_item_write: same actions on both. Server 1's updates[].value also accepts objects and arrays (relation patches); server 2 accepts only scalars.
wit_work_item: server 2 has no continuationToken for list_comments, and its project description says it prompts when project is omitted. Server 1's get runs at organization scope without a project.

repo_pull_request: server 1 adds paging of changed files (skip and top with includeChangedFiles). repo_pull_request_thread_write: server 2's status has a schema default of 'Active', while server 1 has none and allows status on reply.

Identical shapes: pipelines_write, pipelines_run, repo_create_branch, wit_backlog (reorder included), wit_query, work, testplan, wiki_upsert_page and the testplan, work and comment writes. Minor differences: pipelines_build queryOrder is a free string on server 2 and an enum on server 1; repo_file's versionType defaults to Commit for every action on server 2.
uncertain: Whether System.BoardColumn can be written: I believe ADO rejects direct writes and a column move must target WEF_36778208447642C48B0A0F72C104A5C5_Kanban.Column. This is untested: I made no writes and found no past column write in the transcripts. The guard should match both fields.
The Midas board GUID is inferred only from data: that WEF field equals System.BoardColumn in all 71 sampled items. Who owns the other two WEF boards is unknown.
Server 1 is unpinned. Today it is 2.11.0, but a restart of `npx -y @azure-devops/mcp` can pull a newer version with new tools or actions, which is why the guard should fail closed.
repo_pull_request_org: whether ADO's reviewerId search returns PRs where I am a reviewer only through a group. The 'pending' filter drops those PRs either way.
WIQL details I did not run: [Custom.Release#] = '' with '#' in the bracketed name, how '<> @Me' treats unassigned items, and which fields wit_work_item action 'my' returns.
update_build_stage with status 'Run': from ADO docs it starts a manual or skipped stage and does not approve checks. Not tested.
Whether a waiting ManualValidation step shows up in pipelines_build_log list, which could give a rough 'waiting since' time. Untested.
Which state transitionWorkItems moves linked items to depends on ADO process settings. Memory shows it closed #361691.

The agentic-midas band sends its button texts ('Create it.', 'Update it.') as user prompts with asUser:true. Whether UserPromptSubmit hooks see these, and whether they should count as gate approvals, is a design decision for midas-sdlc.

I called no ADO tools, so nothing here was checked against live responses. Facts come from the loaded schemas, the 2.10.0 and 2.11.0 package source, saved work item reads from earlier sessions, and memory. The harness-facts scratchpad folder was not needed.
